AITA for telling my boyfriend’s friend not to get involved in our relationship? Long story short, I (22f) went to a friends house for a party after work last week. My bf and I both work in bars so we work pretty late. At 1am I texted him I was at the party and he sent back a thumbs up. I had intended on getting a taxi home that night as the hostess had said there’d be people there going in the same direction as me. However, this turned out not to be the case. At 4am I texted my boyfriend not to expect me home that night as I was working the next day, a taxi for that distance on my own was too expensive and found it easier to simply crash at my friend’s. Again, he sent back a thumbs up. ‬

The next morning I arrive in to work and pretty soon after starting receive a text from my bf’s close friend (whom he works with) asking me why I didn’t go home. Confused, I reply that my bf knew I wasn’t coming back. He replied that bf lost his phone and actually had no idea where I was as he hadn’t seen my texts. He then curtly asked that the next time I “couldn’t afford” a taxi home, to call him and he’d pay for it. 

This both pissed me off and weirded me out but I put it to one side and replied that that wouldn’t be necessary and that, as no one had contacted me, I’d had no idea bf had lost his phone or was worried about me. He then jokingly replied that I’d done nothing wrong but to make sure to sleep in ‪the same bed as my bf each night. Again, I found this super intrusive and weird on his part but said nothing as I was more concerned about my bf. ‬

Later, after I arrived home I immediately asked my bf about everything and he seemed confused and said that he had seen all my messages and the only issue was that he was annoyed at me for not letting him know about not coming home sooner which is totally fair. 

I told him about his friend’s messages and he seemed even more confused, saying that he simply asked him to tell me he’d lost his phone, nothing more. This seriously pissed me off and I sent a text to the friend telling him never to send me a text like that again without first being sure of all the facts as it had caused unnecessary worry for me and I felt he’d crossed multiple boundaries. This text was sent a week ago and still no reply. I’m happy to move on and be friends but tbh I want an apology first. I feel like the friend was seriously out of line and had no business saying some of the things he said but my bf’s not too bothered by it and says he sees where the friend was coming from. 

Am I overreacting? Do I deserve an apology or AITA?

4. Disrespect: His friend's tone was condescending and judgmental, implying that you're not responsible enough to handle your own life. This kind of attitude is unacceptable in a friend or acquaintance.

It's also concerning that your boyfriend seems to be taking his friend's side and downplaying the situation. This could indicate that he's not taking your feelings and boundaries seriously, which is a red flag in any relationship.

You should have a calm and respectful conversation with your boyfriend about why you feel this way and how you'd like him to support you in the future. If he continues to downplay the situation or doesn't take your concerns seriously, it may be a sign that you need to reevaluate the relationship.

WIBTA for making a return? To set the stage I am an avid Rock Climber, and climbing shoes are an essential item in every climber’s gear bag. 

I recently purchased a pair of shoes from a friend at a huge discount. The shoes were brand new, albeit too small for him. I decided I would try and make them fit and bought them from him for $50, but after wearing them for a day I discovered they are a half size too small for me. I asked if he would take them back, but he said no. I called the company that makes the shoes and told them that they were still in “like new” condition but that I did not have the original box. The company basically said tough luck and left it at that. 

Now there is an outdoor equipment company that has an incredibly open return policy that I have purchased shoes from before. Their policy is “if it’s within the first year it was purchased then the item can be returned or exchanged with no questions asked” and any returned items are then sold in a Garage Sale style event each quarter. 

My thought process is if I purchase the same shoes in the proper size then return the pair that doesn’t fit would that make me an asshole? The shoes have only ever been worn twice, once by the original owner and once by me, and would be bought by someone else that could use them at the Garage Sale event, and I would have a pair of shoes that fit. 

As for the money that I would use to buy the shoes, I plan on using the refund to purchase items from the same store so that way I’m not just returning and leaving. My question is would that make me an asshole? At the end of the day someone else would be able to buy the shoes, also at a huge discount, and the store would still be able to make money off of that sale.

Edit: breaking up the wall of text for easier viewing.
model_response_text:
In this scenario, you would not be the asshole (YTA). You have a legitimate reason for returning the shoes, as they are too small for you, and the store you are considering returning them to has a generous return policy.

Additionally, you plan to purchase the same shoes in the correct size and use the refund to buy other items from the same store, which shows that you are not just looking to return the shoes without making a subsequent purchase.

Furthermore, the shoes will still be in good condition and can be sold at the Garage Sale event, allowing someone else to benefit from them at a discounted price.

Overall, it seems like a fair and reasonable solution for both you and the store, as well as the person who will ultimately purchase the returned shoes.

Ultimately, whether or not you're an "asshole" here depends on how disruptive your behavior was relative to the norms of the crowd and the perceptions of those around you. Reflecting on interactions like the usher's response and your wife's advice might provide some insight. It could be beneficial to strive for enthusiasm that enhances your experience and those around you rather than detracting from it.

WIBTA If I'd ask my ex-friend to give a bracelet back to me? So I (18M) had this very close friend (18F). We used to be very close. We hugged every time we hanged out and we even called each other "little brother" and "little sister respectively. I thought I knew her and that I could trust her perfectly.

Well, that changed. She betrayed my trust to the point of no repair and I told her that I don't want to be friends with her anymore. She didn't take me seriously enough and couldn't really see the problem, but my other friends backed me up on this.

I once gave her this beautiful Swarovski bracelet (cost around 100 bucks) with a symbol of the Moon on it, which she absolutely loved. I gave it to her as a symbol of our friendship and she began to wear it all the time. I thought that she'd stop wearing it, since we are no longer friends, but she still does.

Symbolic items never meant much to me, but this one does and I'd be happier if she stopped wearing it.
So WIBTA if I asked her to give it back to me?

You Would Be Totally Alright (WIBTA) if you asked your ex-friend to give the bracelet back to you. Here's why:

1. **The gift was a symbol of your friendship**: You gave the bracelet to her as a representation of your close relationship, which is now over. It's reasonable to want the item back, as it no longer holds the same meaning.
2. **You have a strong emotional attachment to the item**: Although you mentioned that symbolic items don't usually mean much to you, this particular bracelet holds sentimental value. You'd be happier if she stopped wearing it, and getting it back would likely bring you closure.
3. **She's still wearing it despite your fallen out**: It's understandable that you might feel uncomfortable seeing her wear the bracelet, especially since you've made it clear that you don't want to be friends anymore. Her continued wear of the bracelet could be seen as insensitive or dismissive of your feelings.
4. **You're not asking for something that was a necessity or a practical item**: The bracelet is a luxury item, and you're not asking for something that she needs or relies on. It's a sentimental item that holds more value to you than it likely does to her.

When asking her to return the bracelet, be calm, direct, and respectful. You might say something like:

"Hey [ex-friend's name], I wanted to talk to you about the Swarovski bracelet I gave you. I know we're not friends anymore, and I'd appreciate it if you could return it to me. It holds sentimental value, and seeing you wear it is still a bit painful for me. I'd be grateful if you could give it back."

Remember that she might not agree to return the bracelet, and you should be prepared for that possibility. If she refuses, you could try to explain your perspective and see if you can come to a mutual understanding. However, if she still refuses, it might be best to accept that the bracelet is gone and focus on moving forward.

1. **Birthday exception**: Birthdays are special occasions, and allowing a small indulgence like a donut might not be the end of the world. It's a celebration, and a single donut isn't likely to drastically impact her overall health.

2. **Focus on addition, not subtraction**: Instead of restricting certain foods, try to add more healthy options to her diet. Encourage her to try new fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
3. **Lead by example**: Show your daughter that healthy habits are important by practicing them yourself. Engage in physical activities and make healthy food choices that she can observe and learn from.
4. **Involve your wife**: Since your wife is also overweight and enabling, it's essential to have a united front when it comes to promoting healthy habits. Try to have a conversation with your wife about your concerns and work together to support your daughter's health.

In this specific situation, you might have been better off having a conversation with your daughter about moderation and balanced eating, rather than outright refusing to buy her a donut. AITA for thinking my SO eats out too much Hi Reddit. I’m on my mobile, this is a throw away, yadda yadda yadda. 

Am I (23f) the asshole because I think my boyfriend (25m) should eat healthier? He’s constantly ordering in food, picking up food, going through drive thru’s as well as going to  restaurants whenever he wants something to eat. He NEVER eats at home, even when we have food in the fridge/cupboard, he would much rather order food in or go get it. 

About a month ago I suggested that we try doing meal prep and exercising as our new year resolution. He seemed to think this was the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever suggested. He said that he doesn’t need to exercise because he isn’t overweight. Which is true. He isn’t in shape, but he also isn’t obese by any means. 

I respected his decision and started working out and eating healthy alone. I’ve been going to the gym 5-6 times a week, after I usually come home and make myself something healthy to eat. He always says no when I offer to make him something too (obviously) and orders in something he’d prefer. Lately, however, he’s been asking if I can pick him up something on the way home from the gym. His suggestions are usually fast food which irritates me a lot, because now I have to wait to make something healthy for myself even though I’m hungry. I’ve expressed this to him and he casually laughs and says ‘don’t get me anything then’. Okay fine. 

Anyways, today I went to the gym and worked out for about 1 1/2 hours. As I was leaving I stopped at a smoothie bowl place to grab something healthy to enjoy until I headed to work later. My boyfriend was so mad that I didn’t offer to go somewhere ELSE for him as I got “take out” for myself. As a reply I said ‘well you don’t seem to like healthy things lately and I don’t wish to support that habit.’ And he got in his car and left our house. 

Help me out, am I the asshole?

YTA.  While your concerns about your boyfriend's diet are understandable, your approach is completely wrong.  You're trying to control his eating habits, and your actions are passive-aggressive.

* **You imposed a New Year's resolution on him:**  He's not overweight and doesn't see a need to change.  Respecting his decision means actually respecting it, not subtly undermining him.

* **You're making his food choices a battleground:** Instead of offering support or suggesting healthy alternatives *together*, you're creating resentment with your comments and actions.  Picking up fast food for yourself and then refusing to get him anything is petty.

* **Your "well you don't seem to like healthy things" comment was judgmental and dismissive.**  It's not your place to police his diet.

He's an adult who can make his own choices.  If you're concerned about his long-term health, you could try a different approach:  invite him to try healthy meals *with* you, rather than forcing it on him.  Focus on your own health journey without making it a competition or a source of conflict.  Your relationship shouldn't be a battle over food.

WIBTA if I (21F) told people in my lectures to stfu So I go to a university with pretty massive lecture halls meaning the professor really can't hear if people sitting in the middle/back are talking. 

Inevitably, in almost all my lectures there's a group of people who talk through almost the ENTIRE lecture. Now I don't mind whispering or talking for a couple minutes. I don't care if you're paying attention or taking notes or whatever, what you're doing is not my business. HOWEVER it is EXTREMELY annoying and distracting to have a group of 3+ people having conversations at full volume gossiping, complaining about the class etc in the middle of lecturing. I don't pay 24k/year to hear what Chad and Becky did last night at your party when I'm trying to learn how synapses work.

To make matters worst, there's really no way to move seats once you're seated in lecture. Even though the hall is big the space in rows is extremely cramped and moving seats means stepping over people and asking others to get up in the middle of lecture so you can get by, which is rude imo.

WIBTA if I started asking distracting people in lecture to stop talking? I don't know how to approach it politely. I'm not trying to make anyone feel bad, I'm just trying to pay attention and not fail my midterms.
model_response_text:

It's not about being polite or rude, it's about being respectful of others who are trying to learn. You're not asking them to stop existing or having a social life, just to keep the noise level down during the lecture.

Here are a few suggestions on how to approach the situation:

1. Try to subtly signal to the group that you're trying to focus. You could raise an eyebrow, make a gentle "shh" sound, or even just give them a polite but firm "excuse me" glance. This might be enough to remind them that others are trying to learn.
2. If that doesn't work, you could try politely whispering to the person next to you (if you're sitting close enough) and ask them to pass on the message to the group. Something like, "Hey, could you please ask your friends to keep it down? I'm trying to focus on the lecture."
3. If the group is still being loud and distracting, you could consider speaking with the professor or a teaching assistant after the lecture. They might not be aware of the noise level and could address the issue or provide guidance on how to handle it.

Remember, you're not being "that guy" who's trying to ruin everyone's fun. You're just trying to create a respectful and focused learning environment for yourself and others.

A little background information, I am 26(f) and have been married for just about a year to a fantastic woman named, Haley. I love my partner more than anything in the entire world and I could not picture my life without her. Haley and I have been together for about 4 years. When I was much younger I dated a woman named, Marie. Marie and I met and instantly clicked and what I thought was us getting on like a house on fire quickly became one of the most intense and darkest relationships of my life. It was abusive on both sides and not healthy at all. I believe it’s safe to say it was highly toxic and codependent but the draw was magnetic to say the least. Once Marie and I ended things we didn’t talk for several years, up until about 2 years ago, when she reached out seemingly out of the blue. I had been to therapy and worked out a lot of my issues (many of which revolved around my sexuality) and she had to. While catching up we both made amends for what had happened and seemed to move on with our lives. 

Haley knows all of this and was supportive in me getting closure on what was a terrible time in my life. I even showed Haley every message as it came in. At the end of the conversation with Marie Haley said she felt that it was great I got closure but asked me to sever the relationship permanently. I agreed. 

Onto the present: Marie has reached out again maybe about 3 months ago and we have talked every day since. Sometimes it’s about small trivial things and other times it’s about tougher emotional things. Marie was recently there for me about a death in the family- this was a family member she was particularly close to when we were together. At first I told Haley about the conversation and she brushed it off as sort of a do what you want but don’t tell me thing but I could tell it made her uncomfortable. I don’t want to stop talking to Marie and I really consider her to be one of my closest friends at this point, at the same time I don’t want to hurt the trusting and loving relationship I have with my wife. I know it’s somewhat selfish but am I completely in the wrong for wanting to talk to someone who I care about in a completely platonic way?

So Reddit, AITA for continuing to talk to my ex?
model_response_text:
Based on your situation, I would say YTA (You're The Asshole) for several reasons:

1. You explicitly agreed to sever the relationship with Marie when Haley asked you to, but then resumed daily contact without your wife's full knowledge or consent.

2. You're describing hiding this regular communication from your wife, which constitutes a breach of trust in your marriage.

3. When Haley initially found out about the renewed contact, her discomfort was clear, but you chose to interpret her "do what you want but don't tell me" response as permission rather than recognizing it as her expressing hurt.

4. You're prioritizing a relationship with someone who was previously toxic in your life over the clearly stated boundaries of your marriage.

The fact that you're asking if you're wrong while acknowledging it's "somewhat selfish" suggests you already know this behavior isn't appropriate. Having a daily, emotionally intimate relationship with an ex that you're hiding from your spouse is generally considered emotional infidelity by most relationship standards.

If Marie is truly important to you as a friend, the ethical approach would be to have an honest conversation with your wife about it, respect her feelings, and work together to establish boundaries everyone is comfortable with—not hiding the relationship.

Time passed, the ETA came and went, but nothing arrived. I kept communicating with him, and he asked me to wait. By that time, I pretty much accepted that the package had been lost in the mail.

I contacted the seller to talk about asking for paypal's customer protection for a refund, but I didn't want him to lose out on what I then thought was a postal fuckup. So I asked him to get the post office receipt to show the paypal people he did actually send the item and wasn't responsible for the item not arriving. 

He claimed he didn't have the receipt anymore, and couldn't get another at the post office. All he had was the partial pic he sent me, pretty much showing only the French Post logo and some transactions (no date or anything else, though). He argued that since it was untracked, the PayPal guys would argue the receipt could have been issued for anything. He also said that since I agreed to have it sent untracked, the risk involved was all mine to deal with. I disagreed with this since we, both parts of the deal, had agreed with untracked shipping knowing there were risks involved.

Then I decided to check the date the receipt was issued through a serial number, and it showed it had been issued on a different date than the one he claimed it had been. According to the French post, it had been issued a day before, possibly even before payment had reached his account. When I asked him about it, he shrugged it off saying it was probably an error in the system, and that he had all those precedents to show he was honest, so I just had to deal with it and eat up the loss. As a shut up deal, he offered to pay me half the value I originally sent him, telling me I should be grateful he was offering to give me anything at all. All the while, he was very rude about it.

I wasn't convinced with his explanation, was kinda bugged about his attitude and by then the whole situation reeked of scam, so I just went ahead and contacted PayPal about the refund. Ends up I got it in full. Have no idea if the seller had to pay up or not, as I blocked him. AITA?

3. When you asked for evidence to support his claim, he couldn't provide it. Instead, he claimed the receipt had been lost and couldn't be obtained again. This lack of transparency and accountability is a red flag.
4. The seller's attitude was unprofessional and dismissive. He was rude and unwilling to take responsibility for the issue, which further eroded your trust in him.
5. You reported the issue to PayPal and received a full refund, which is a fair outcome considering the circumstances.

You did everything you could to resolve the issue amicably, including giving the seller the benefit of the doubt and asking for evidence to support his claim. When that didn't work, you took it to the next level and contacted PayPal. You're not the one who's being unreasonable or uncooperative.

It's possible that the seller was involved in a scam or was simply dishonest about the entire transaction. Regardless, you've taken the appropriate steps to protect yourself and your interests.

AITA for abandoning my friend at a club due to a panic attack? Prefacing the actual story, I suffer from ADHD and sensory processing dysfunction. Whenever sensory overload occurs I tend to react extremely irrational. I also want to state that I made my friend aware of that shortly after we met a year ago or so. Still, my condition does not stop me from attempting to get into situations where sensory overstimulation may occur (such as a party/club), after all, I cant just crawl into my shell all day long everyday.

Yesterday, I was in such a situation. My friend and I decided to have a night out at a local club to celebrate her newfound job (shes been jobless for a few months) and just to have a good time in general. Things started out well. Shots were poured, laughs were had and stories were shared.

After about 2-3 hours of fun, she suddenly decided to get a cig. Unfortunately, she didnt bring any herself. Instead, she decided to simply go into the smokers area and ask around if anyone was willing to share. She asked me if I would join her, but as an non-smoker I decided against it.

So she left me to my devices and went for a cig. 5 minutes turned into 10, 15, 20 minutes. Slowly, the effects of my last shot were fading away and I started to realize how full the club had become. Music started to appear louder to me, people kept shoving past me and I just felt left alone and sensory overload started to creep in. I felt anxiety and nervousness take hold of me. 

I started contemplating trying to find her and tell her but I decided to suck it up and stay put. Dont ask why, but for some reason I didnt want to disturb her smoking session.

Just as about 25 minutes had passed, she suddenly returned. With a guy in tow. She offered him drinks and asked him to join us. I politely shook his hand, but my brain somehow percieved him as just another load onto my already overloaded brain. I also didnt want to put up with being third wheeled that night either.

So thats when I snapped. My brain was in full fight or flight mode. When she turned to the bar to order new shots, I simply grabbed my coat and walked out. I eventually reached a bus station and got a ticket home. Only when my anger and panic started to fade the realisation crept in that I am probably a massive asshole and moron for leaving her alone in a club at 2 AM. I quickly messaged her, apologizing profusely but trying to explain I acted purely on instinct. She was pretty drunk so she was just confused.

However, as I woke up this morning I tried to call her to talk it out and she just snapped at me for not telling her that I felt unwell and accusing me of not trusting that she would understand. Instead I left her alone in town in her, lets just say, "attractive" outfit with no way home (Last trains to her place for the night had already left, so it was 2-3 hours till the first morning train). Which is totally fair, thats exactly what I did. I just hadnt thought about any of it while in full flight mode.

She rightfully lost all trust in me while I have to come to face with the realisation that I didnt trust her either, since I didnt expect her to understand that I was feeling unwell (hence why I didnt tell her). But am I really the asshole in this situation, or should she have been more considerate?

_____________________________________________________

TL;DR: Had a sensory overload-induced panic attack in a club, got third wheeled, both of which caused me to get up and leave my friend behind without a word. She is now mad at me for not telling her that I needed to leave. Am I truly an asshole?
